What the circuit is thinking about.

Read the evidence packs
Public Forum (PF)PF-2026

Arctic military & geopolitical posture

“Resolved: The United States federal government should substantially increase its military presence in the Arctic.”

2v2 team debate on sovereignty, NATO treaties, polar shipping channels, and ecological preservation.

Lincoln-Douglas (LD)LD-2026

Wealth taxation & distributive justice

“Resolved: The United States ought to adopt a wealth tax to remediate systemic economic inequality.”

1v1 philosophical clash grounding deontological rights, Rawlsian fairness, and constitutional tax authority.

Congressional & OratoryCONG-01

Civic discourse & legislative simulation

“Bills on artificial intelligence governance, rural health subsidies, and student mental health resources.”

Chamber debate with formal parliamentary procedure and original persuasive speeches.

Why this work matters

A room to think out loud.

Debate gives students a practical way to research the world, test their convictions, and learn from someone who sees the same question differently.

Curiosity before certainty.
01

Make the case.

Research, framing, and evidence are taught as habits of mind, not just tournament tricks.

02

Find your voice.

Students practice speaking clearly, listening closely, and refining their perspectives with intention.

03

Build the room.

A chapter is a durable school community with coaching resources, scrimmages, and a place to return to.

04

Keep the door open.

Free open-source materials make serious debate available to any school community.

For students, teachers, and people who still have questions

Bring a better question to the room.

We provide the curriculum, starter kits, and practice scrimmage pairings. Your school brings the curiosity.
